extracted.intended_audience: university technology transfer administrators, university contracting officers, faculty and administrators negotiating or managing federal research contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on rights in technical data and computer software under federal (FAR/DFARS) awards, including definitions, categories of government rights, key FAR/DFARS clauses and alternates, marking/notice requirements, and negotiation considerations for universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Data (FAR 52.227-14(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Data is 'recorded information, regardless of form or the media on which it may be recorded.' The term includes technical data and computer software. Technical data are 'data which are of a scientific or technical nature.' The clause also defines categories such as 'form, fit and function' data (sufficient to enable physical and functional interchangeability and identifying source, size, configuration, and other characteristics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand these definitions since they determine what falls under FAR data rights (technical data vs. computer software; form/fit/function data are treated specially).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of FAR Data Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR identifies multiple rights: unlimited rights (government may use, disclose, reproduce, prepare derivative works, distribute copies to the public, perform and display publicly, in any manner and for any purpose); limited rights (as set forth in a limited rights notice in paragraph (g)(2)); and restricted rights (rights in restricted computer software, as set forth in this clause or collateral agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the legal consequences of each rights category when negotiating delivery, marking, and licensing for data/software in contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of Rights to FAR Data (FAR 52.227-14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The government receives unlimited rights to: (1) data first produced in performance of the contract; (2) form, fit, and function data delivered under the contract; (3) manuals/instructional/training material for installation, operation, routine maintenance; and (4) all other data delivered under the contract not marked with a limited or restricted rights legend. Contractors retain rights to use, publish, protect, correct, and claim copyright in some data first produced in performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check which deliverables are subject to unlimited rights and mark deliverables appropriately; inclusion of Alternate IV can allow contractor copyright/ownership assertions but government retains a paid-up, nonexclusive, irrevocable worldwide license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data First Produced or Delivered — Publication & Copyright (FAR 52.227-14(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor may establish copyright in scientific and technical articles that contain 'data first produced in the performance of the contract' and published in academic/technical/professional journals without prior approval; prior express written approval required to establish copyright in other data. 'First produced' means not previously existing in any form (including software). Agencies may request advance copies for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities can typically publish articles without prior approval, but must seek permission to claim copyright in other data; plan ahead and provide advance copies if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate IV (FAR) — Research Performed Solely by Universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternate IV is to be used in contracts for basic or applied research to be performed solely by universities/colleges. It provides blanket permission for universities to claim copyright without limitation in any data first produced in performance. When asserting copyright under Alternate IV, universities must acknowledge government sponsorship (including contract number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate IV is critical for universities wishing to assert copyright in contract-generated data; it cannot be used when the contract purpose is development of software for public distribution, and contracting-officer permission is required if non-university parties are performing work. Ensure Alternate IV is included where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government License Even if Copyright Is Perfected
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfecting a copyright claim in data first produced and delivered to the government still obligates the contractor to provide the federal government a paid-up, nonexclusive, irrevocable worldwide license to reproduce, prepare derivative works, distribute copies to the public, and perform/display publicly, by or on behalf of the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with copyright, universities must recognize and plan for the government's broad license; for software, if copyright is perfected the government may not have the right to distribute copies to the public (contrast with other data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Security & Publication Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor rights may be limited by export control or national security laws/regulations or by contract language. FAR 27.404(g)(2) states no restrictions may be placed on conduct/reporting of unclassified research in university contracts except as provided by statute; accepting publication restrictions may cause loss of the fundamental research exemption under export control regs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should carefully review contract data rights clauses to avoid accepting publication restrictions that could violate FAR policy or export control rules and compromise fundamental research exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Not First Produced in Contract Performance (FAR 52.227-14(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Data created outside federal sponsorship (pre-existing, third-party, student coursework, industrial contracts) that are delivered to the government require sorting of copyright, ownership, and license rights prior to delivery. Permission is needed from the government before delivering such non-first-produced data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure rights clearance for embedded pre-existing or third-party data/software before delivery; negotiate with the government to avoid granting unlimited license rights to such data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited Rights Data (FAR 52.227-14(a) & (g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited rights data (other than computer software) are those that embody trade secrets or are commercial/financial and confidential or privileged, to the extent they pertain to items, components, or processes developed at private expense. Under Alternate II (or I), limited rights may allow government internal use but restrict disclosure/manufacture; Alternate I has a different definition that may allow withholding more data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities must identify and mark limited rights data (and deliver form/fit/function data in lieu if withholding) and use Alternates I/II appropriately; failure to identify/protect such data can result in government acquiring unlimited rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted Computer Software (FAR 52.227-14(a) & Alternate III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricted computer software is software developed at private expense that is a trade secret, is commercial/financial and confidential/privileged, or is published copyrighted software. Computer databases are treated as limited rights data. Under Alternate III, a restricted rights notice gives the government more limited rights than a limited rights notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before delivery, determine government restricted rights in software via the clause or negotiation; for published software a copyright notice may be presumed to license the government unless marked 'unpublished with rights reserved.'

rubrics_metrics.name: When Government May Require Delivery of Limited/Restricted Data (Alternates II & III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternates II and III enable the government to require delivery of a contractor’s limited rights data or restricted computer software rather than allow the contractor to withhold them. FAR lists justifications/purposes for such disclosure (e.g., use by support service contractors, evaluation by nongovernment evaluators, use by other contractors in the government’s program, emergency repair, release to a foreign government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect contracting officers to add alternates or modify clauses during performance to require delivery if necessary; negotiate specific exceptions where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor Modifications to Limited/Restricted Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor modifications to limited rights data or restricted computer software are included in the definitions of limited/restricted data and therefore will not necessarily subject these modifications to unlimited government rights, even if first developed in performance of a government contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in characterizing modifications as 'minor' and document provenance and expense basis to preserve restrictive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of Limited Rights Data/Restricted Software (FAR 52.227-15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 52.227-15 requests offerors to identify limited rights data or restricted computer software in response to solicitations. Inclusion may signal anticipated need for such deliveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the solicitation response stage to identify and protect limited/restricted data; failing to mark at this stage may make later protection difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in Data: Special Works (FAR 52.227-17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The special works clause is for contracts intended for production/compilation of data (e.g., audiovisual works) and grants the government unlimited rights to data delivered and first produced. Release/publication of data first produced requires government written permission; contractors may not claim copyright without permission and must indemnify the government for liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should avoid accepting the special works clause as it conflicts with common institutional policies and may violate FAR provisions protecting fundamental research; carefully check solicitations to avoid inadvertently accepting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in Data: Existing Works (FAR 52.227-18) and Commercial Software (FAR 52.227-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.227-18 acquires nonexclusive worldwide license for existing audiovisual and similar works and includes indemnification. FAR 52.227-19 is used to acquire computer programs/databases developed at private expense; government generally has rights to use, copy, reproduce, modify, adapt, and disclose to support service contractors. If software includes a copyright notice it is presumed licensed to the government unless contract states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities rarely should accept these clauses without careful review because of indemnification and broad license terms; explicitly negotiate exceptions where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR Data Rights (FAR 52.227-20)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.227-20 applies to SBIR programs and recognizes an SBIR rights in data notice. It permits the SBIR firm to assert copyright ownership of FAR data created and to label data as SBIR data unless contract requires unrestricted delivery. The clause limits government disclosure/use outside the government for four years after acceptance of all deliverables, after which nondisclosure protections lapse though government retains limited rights to use for government purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities acting as SBIR subcontractors should understand the four-year nondisclosure window and ensure subcontracting provisions secure rights from subcontractors to provide required government rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to Proposal Technical Data (FAR 52.227-23)
rubrics_metrics.description: This clause gives the government unlimited rights to all technical data contained in the proposal upon which the contract is based, unless the contractor specifically identifies pages containing confidential information to be exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully identify and mark confidential proposal pages to avoid relinquishing unlimited rights inadvertently; contrast with DFARS approaches which may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFARS — Source-of-Funds Allocation Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike FAR, DFARS allocates rights by the 'source of funds' used to develop DOD technical data: (1) developed exclusively with government funds; (2) developed with mixed funding; (3) developed exclusively at private expense; and (4) specifically negotiated rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working on DOD contracts, determine the funding source for development costs since DFARS rights attach to funding origin rather than statement of work/deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Technical Data Developed Exclusively with Government Funds (DFARS 252.227-7013[b][1])
rubrics_metrics.description: If data are developed exclusively with government funds (costs paid in whole by government or required for performance), the government is entitled to unlimited rights (use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, disclose in any manner and for any purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid charging development costs to indirect pools or other university funds if you intend to preserve contractor rights; consider Alternate I (relinquish) only with care — it allows contractor to publish within 24 months to obtain publication rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Technical Data Developed with Mixed Funding (DFARS 252.227-7013[b][2])
rubrics_metrics.description: When data are developed partly with non-government funds, data are considered mixed funding and the government obtains 'government purpose rights' (GPR): use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display within government without restriction and outside for government purposes. GPR typically lasts five years (or negotiated period), after which government receives unlimited rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware GPR begins at contract execution (not at data creation) and is often only five years — consider negotiating a longer period when commercialization will require more time; GPR may extend across agencies and to contractor use under NDA.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOD Technical Data Developed Exclusively at Private Expense (DFARS 252.227-7013[b][3])
rubrics_metrics.description: Data developed exclusively at private expense entitles the government only to limited rights if the data are marked with the prescribed limited rights legend; limited rights allow government internal use but generally prohibit disclosure outside government or use for manufacture except in limited circumstances (e.g., emergency repair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark DOD technical data with the required limited rights legend and justify restricted markings; treat indirect cost pools as private funding where appropriate to preserve limited rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifically Negotiated Rights (DFARS 252.227-7013[b][4])
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may negotiate alternative license rights for any of the funding categories, but the government cannot receive lesser rights than it would under limited rights. DFARS prescribes specific legends for each rights category and requires justification for restricted markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negotiation to tailor rights where possible, but expect DFARS to be prescriptive about legends and to require justification of restrictive markings; compare with FAR which is less prescriptive about placement of notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFARS Rights in Noncommercial (and Commercial) Computer Software (252.227-7014) — Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: DFARS defines computer software broadly to include programs, source code, object code, design details, algorithms, processes, flow charts, formulae and related material enabling reproduction/recompilation. Computer software does not include databases or documentation (documentation defined separately as manuals, installation/operating instructions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify deliverables correctly (software vs. databases vs. documentation) under DFARS to determine applicable clauses and rights; these classifications affect whether data are treated under 7013 (technical data) or 7014 (software).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking, Legends, and Justification Requirements (DFARS vs FAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: DFARS is prescriptive about specific legends for government purpose rights, limited rights, and specifically negotiated rights and requires contractors to justify the validity of restrictive markings (252.227-7013(f)-(g)). FAR prescribes content of limited rights notice but is less prescriptive about placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DFARS marking and justification rules strictly for DOD contracts; for FAR contracts, ensure limited/restricted notices meet clause requirements and are properly affixed to data to preserve rights.
